ai.description: This 35–45 cm lizard features a spiny dorsal crest and brownish-grey scales. Males display bright red throats and black facial markings during breeding. It is distinguished by its elongated, slender tail.
ai.identificationRemarks: The most reliable cue is the presence of two distinct, separated spines above the tympanum, which distinguishes *Calotes versicolor* from similar Indian agamid species.
ai.habitat: *Calotes versicolor* inhabits diverse environments across the Indian subcontinent, ranging from tropical forests and scrublands to urban gardens up to 2,000 meters altitude.
ai.behavior: The Changeable Lizard is diurnal and territorial, often displaying its bright red throat and head during mating season or when defending its home range from rivals.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Calotes versicolor* is oviparous, laying clutches of 5–20 eggs in soil burrows. Breeding occurs primarily from April to September, peaking during the monsoon season.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Calotes versicolor* is widely distributed across the Indian subcontinent, ranging from sea level up to 2,000 meters in diverse habitats across almost all Indian states.
